subject: english-literature
title: Sound Effects of Language
welcome_lead: Some devices work on the ear as much as the mind.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on alliteration, onomatopoeia and sound devices.
final_note: You can now hear how writers tune their sentences.

concepts.def: Same starting sound on nearby words.
Word that sounds like its meaning.
Same end sound on two words.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Slithering, silent serpents' uses alliteration — repeated starting sound builds rhythm or mood.
'Crash', 'buzz', 'hiss' — words that sound like what they describe. Comic books love them.
Sibilance uses 's' or soft 'sh' sounds. It can suggest secrets, snakes or whispers.

numericals.q: How many sound devices are listed (alliteration, onomatopoeia, assonance, sibilance, plosive)?

free_texts.q: A word that sounds like its meaning is called ____.
